implemented_capabilities.notes: A real variable-length Cypher query (CAN_ACCESS*1..8 with all(access IN relationships(path) WHERE access.active = true), ORDER BY hops LIMIT 50) over a hard-coded 11-node synthetic cloud graph seeded by SEED_CYPHER. The engine pattern is real; the cloud data is demo-only and no cloud ingest exists.

implemented_capabilities.capability: What-if remediation by deactivating edges and re-querying
implemented_capabilities.notes: Sets CAN_ACCESS.active=false on one of two allow-listed edges then reruns the path query to show residual risk; recommendations are filtered to edges present in active paths. Only two hard-coded fixes are modeled.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Public website discovery scan with SSRF controls
implemented_capabilities.notes: Bounded same-origin crawler (12 pages, 1 MB cap, 20 first-party scripts, ports 80/443 only) with public-IP DNS check, manual redirect handling that never follows off-origin hops, passive security-header findings, and route extraction from JS source.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Runtime page-load behaviour pass (Playwright) with request blocking
implemented_capabilities.notes: Headless Chromium route interception blocks off-origin, XHR/WebSocket and non-GET/HEAD requests and records popup/navigation signals; degrades to status 'unavailable' if Playwright is missing.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Traffic-signal classification and HAR/OpenAPI/SARIF evidence import
implemented_capabilities.notes: Host/path substring heuristics label advertising/analytics/payment etc. with low or medium confidence and an honest 'not proof' reason string; credential-like query params are redacted before persistence. Compound-TLD list is a tiny hard-coded set, not the public suffix list.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Per-site persisted scan graphs with scan-to-scan diff
implemented_capabilities.notes: Each host gets its own FalkorDB graph (pathguard_site_<sha256[:20]>); every scan creates Scan nodes chained with (old)-[:PRECEDES]->(new) and Route/ApiEndpoint/Dependency/Interaction/Finding nodes whose edges carry scan_id, active, mechanism and evidence strings. changes = set difference (added/removed) of routes, APIs, findings, interactions versus the previous scan.

Question category is chosen by keyword matching (finding/popup/dependency/api); summaries are template strings with optional OpenAI rewrite. simulate_site_remediation flips Finding.active and its HAS_FINDING edge to false.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Optional LLM summary of graph evidence
implemented_capabilities.notes: Calls the OpenAI Responses API only to paraphrase path evidence in 3 sentences. The site variant references an undefined name 'result' (agent.py:216) and would raise NameError when OPENAI_API_KEY is set.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Two-tier service split (app API -> Graph API -> FalkorDB)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Only graph_api imports falkordb; the application backend talks HTTP via urllib to a separate service and returns 503 with no fallback store.

graph_models_and_cypher: Demo graph 'pathguard': Principal, Endpoint, Workload, Identity, Secret, DataStore, DataAsset(classification) with CAN_ACCESS{id,mechanism,evidence,active}. Site graphs 'pathguard_site_<hash>': Site, Scan, Route, ApiEndpoint, Dependency, Interaction, Finding, Principal; edges HAS_SCAN, PRECEDES, HAS_ROUTE, CONTAINS, CAN_REACH, OBSERVED_PUBLIC, CALLS, LOADS, OBSERVED_INTERACTION, HAS_FINDING (all with id, scan_id, active, mechanism, evidence). Cypher is built by string interpolation using a json.dumps-based literal escaper (store.py:_literal) instead of query parameters. Patterns: variable-length path with all() predicate on relationships, list comprehensions over nodes/relationships, MERGE upserts with SET, SET ... active=false for simulated removal. No APOC/GDS; pure openCypher so FalkorDB-compatible.
algorithms: Bounded variable-length reachability CAN_ACCESS*1..8 filtered on active edges, ordered by hop count in graph_api/store.py:PATH_QUERY
Edge-deactivation what-if with recomputation of residual paths in store.py:simulate_revocation and agent.py:simulate
Snapshot diff (set difference of routes/APIs/findings/interactions between consecutive scans) in store.py:ingest_site_scan/_site_inventory
Bounded same-origin BFS crawl with public-IP check and manual redirect hop recording in scanner.py:scan_website/_fetch
Heuristic role classification via substring patterns with confidence labels in scanner.py:_classify_interaction
backend_interfaces: App API: GET /api/health, GET /api/overview, POST /api/investigate, POST /api/remediate, POST /api/reset, POST /api/sites/scan, POST /api/sites/question, GET /api/sites/history, GET /api/sites/scan, POST /api/sites/remediate, /graph-api/docs proxy

Graph API: GET /v1/health, GET /v1/analysis, GET /v1/query, POST /v1/remediate, POST /v1/reset, POST /v1/sites/scan, POST /v1/sites/question, GET /v1/sites/history, GET /v1/sites/scan, POST /v1/sites/remediate
frontend_interfaces: React/Vite single-page console (frontend/src/App.jsx): Sidebar, GraphView (subgraph from paths), PathCard, TrafficSignals, SummaryCards, WebsiteScanView, EmptyGraphState
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: PathguardAgent is a constrained pipeline (keyword guard on the question -> graph query -> template summary -> optional LLM paraphrase); no autonomous loop and no persistent agent memory beyond the stored scan history graph.
security_findings: graph_api/store.py:113-115,155-308,333-352,401-471 - Cypher built by f-string concatenation with a custom json.dumps literal escaper rather than parameters; site_host is regex-limited (store.py:148) but scan_id/finding_id/question-derived values rely solely on _literal escaping
graph_api/store.py:542-545 - f-string Cypher with edge_id, protected by REMEDIATION_EDGE_IDS allow-list (not injectable)
graph_api/store.py:352 and :468 - f-string relationship type/label from fixed internal dict/tuple (not injectable)

graph_api/main.py:114-117 - POST /v1/sites/scan accepts an arbitrary dict[str, Any] snapshot and indexes it with hard keys (KeyError -> 500); no authentication on the Graph API (intended as internal, bound to 127.0.0.1 in docker-compose.yml)
backend/main.py:115-117 and :161-163 - /api/reset and /api/sites/remediate mutate graph state with no authentication

backend/scanner.py:54-63,154 - SSRF guard resolves DNS then urllib resolves again at connect time (DNS-rebinding TOCTOU window); only 80/443 and public IPs allowed, off-origin redirects never followed

backend/scanner.py:288-495 - launches headless Chromium that executes first-party JavaScript from an arbitrary user-supplied public URL (browser-escape/resource risk; compensated by request interception and container hardening in docker-compose.yml)
backend/agent.py:216 - undefined variable 'result' inside static method _optional_site_model_summary: NameError when OPENAI_API_KEY is set (functional bug)
backend/agent.py:142,170-175,193,229-234 - OPENAI_API_KEY read from env; scan evidence (URLs, paths) sent to api.openai.com; no hard-coded secrets found
backend/graph_client.py:20-32 - unauthenticated urllib calls to GRAPH_API_URL (default http://graph-api:8100)
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps attack-path / exposure-to-sensitive-data analysis (same family as Argus-SOC attack paths), what-if remediation simulation, and web-surface dependency inventory. Snapshot diffing overlaps supply/dependency drift ideas.
evidence_drift_relevance: MEDIUM - every edge carries evidence text, scan_id and an active flag, scans are chained with PRECEDES and diffed run-to-run, and edge deactivation re-derives residual paths (a primitive form of dependency invalidation), but there is no supersession model, validity intervals or approval gating.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Compact FalkorDB-compatible pattern for evidence-bearing reachability, active-flag what-if invalidation, and PRECEDES-chained snapshot diffing that can be generalized to evidence-drift scans.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB; Playwright/Chromium only for the optional runtime scan; OpenAI key optional

strategy_rationale: The attack-path and what-if remediation queries plus snapshot diff form a self-contained security capability, but the seed data is a hard-coded demo and Cypher is string-built, so port the patterns with parameterized queries rather than the module. No license file and no tests.
